Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Shekhar Kumar Yadav,J.
1.

Heard learned counsel for the applicant and learned Additional Government Advocate for the
State.

2. This anticipatory bail application (under Section 438 Cr.P.C.) has been moved seeking bail in
Crime No.122 of 2018, under Sections 498A, 304 B Ipc and 3/4 Dp Act, Police Station Bela, District
Auraiya.

3.  In short, the prosecution story is that on 1005.2018 at around 9 am in the morning, the accused Shri Chandra and Duli Chandra, brother-in-law Pappu poured kerosene oil on the daughter of first informant, namely, Sundari, thereafter, the accused persons took her to the CHC Bela in burn condition from where she was referred to Medical College where during treatment she died.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicants submits that the applicants have been falsely implicated in the present case, in fact, no such incident has taken place.
The applicants have never committed any offence as alleged in the impugned FIR.
The applicant is brother-in-law (devar) of the deceased and living separately since 2017 i.e. before the alleged incident.
He has never demanded for any additional dowry nor he has harassed the deceased.
As per allegation, main role assigned to the husband of the deceased.
As per postmortem report, cause of death has been mentioned as Asphyxia as a result of antemortem.

During investigation, no credible evidence was found against the applicant, hence, the investigating officer has not submitted charge sheet against the applicant but the trial court summoned the applicant under Section 319 Cr.P.C. ignoring all above aspects.
From the perusal of the impugned FIR, no offence is made out against the applicant but the court below in a routine manner summoned the applicant.
The applicant is having no previous criminal history as has been mentioned in paragraph 36 of the affidavit filed in support of the application.
5. Learned AGA has vehemently opposed the prayer for grant of anticipatory bail to the applicant.
6. From the perusal of impugned FIR as well as material brought on record and looking into the facts of the case, at this stage, it cannot be said that no offence is made out against the applicant.

7. After having heard the learned counsel for the parties present and perused the order sheet of the court below as well as material brought on record and also keeping in view the fact that the applicants are continuously absconding from the proceedings, there is no justification for granting anticipatory bail to the applicants.
8. Accordingly, the present anticipatory bail application is dismissed.

9. However considering the facts and circumstances of the case, it is directed that in case the applicant appears before the court below and seeks grant of bail, his application shall be heard and decided expeditiously in accordance with law.

Order Date :- 16.5.2024 Ajeet  Dulichandra vs State Of Up Another on 16 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/83596883/
